title: Divisor Count Of Number
description: Return the number of positive divisors of `n` (including `1` and `n`).

title: Least Common Multiple Pair
description: Return the least common multiple of the two positive integers `a` and `b`.
constraints: the result fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Reversed Number Value
description: Reverse the decimal digits of the positive integer `n` and return the resulting integer (trailing zeros of `n` disappear, e.g. `120` becomes `21`).
constraints: the reversed value fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Harshad Number Check
description: A positive integer is a Harshad number if it is divisible by the sum of its own digits. Return `true` if `n` is a Harshad number.

title: Trailing Zero Bits Count
description: Return the number of trailing zero bits in the binary representation of `n` (for example `8 = 1000` has three).
constraints: count zeros from the least significant bit up to the first set bit

title: Largest Power Of Two Not Above
description: Return the largest power of two that is less than or equal to `n`.

examples.explanation: The largest power of two not above n is 8.
The largest power of two not above n is 16.

title: Longest Binary Ones Run
description: Return the length of the longest block of consecutive `1` bits in the binary representation of `n` (`0` if `n = 0`).

examples.explanation: The longest run of ones has length 3.
The longest run of ones has length 0.

constraints: use the plain binary form without leading zeros

title: Odd Bit Parity Check
description: Return `true` if the binary representation of `n` contains an odd number of `1` bits.
constraints: only the count of set bits matters

title: Reverse Eight Bits
description: Write `n` as an 8-bit binary number (with leading zeros), reverse the order of the 8 bits and return the resulting integer.

title: Xor Of Stepped Sequence
description: Build the array `a` with `a[i] = start + 2 * i` for `0 <= i < n` and return the bitwise XOR of all its elements.

examples.explanation: The XOR of the sequence is 8.
The XOR of the sequence is 8.

title: Collatz Steps To One
description: Starting from `n`, repeat: if the number is even divide it by `2`, otherwise replace it by `3 * number + 1`. Return the number of steps needed to reach `1`.
constraints: the sequence always reaches 1 for these inputs

title: Sum Of Two Squares Check
description: Return `true` if `n` can be written as `a * a + b * b` for some non-negative integers `a` and `b`.
constraints: a and b may be zero

title: Anti-Diagonal Total
description: `grid` is an `n x n` table stored row by row. Return the sum of the cells on the anti-diagonal (from the top-right corner to the bottom-left corner).

title: Heaviest Row Index
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. Return the index of the row with the largest sum; if several rows tie, return the smallest index.

title: Transposed Weighted Sum
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. Let `T` be its transpose (a `C x R` table, `T[i][j] = grid[j][i]`). Return the sum of `T[i][j] * (i + 1) * (j + 1)` over all cells of `T`.

title: Cells Above Both Averages
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. Count the cells whose value is strictly greater than the average of their row and also strictly greater than the average of their column.

title: Reshaped Cell Lookup
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. Reshape it, keeping the row-by-row order of the elements, into an `r x c` table. If this is impossible (`R * C != r * c`) return `-1`; otherwise return the value in row `i`, column `j` of the reshaped table.

examples.explanation: The requested value is 4 (-1 means the reshape is impossible).
The requested value is -1 (-1 means the reshape is impossible).

constraints: 1 <= R, C, r, c <= 100, grid.length = R * C

title: Identity Matrix Check
description: `grid` is an `n x n` table stored row by row. Return `true` if it is the identity matrix (ones on the main diagonal and zeros everywhere else).

title: Upper Triangular Check
description: `grid` is an `n x n` table stored row by row. Return `true` if every cell below the main diagonal is `0` (the matrix is upper triangular).

title: Empty Rows And Columns Count
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. Return the number of rows that contain only zeros plus the number of columns that contain only zeros.

examples.explanation: There are 3 all-zero lines in total.
There are 0 all-zero lines in total.

title: Excess Divisor Sum Numbers
description: A number is abundant if the sum of its proper divisors (divisors smaller than itself) is greater than the number. Return how many abundant numbers lie in `1..n`.

examples.explanation: There are 1 abundant number(s) up to n.
There are 0 abundant number(s) up to n.

constraints: proper divisors exclude the number itself

title: Smallest Prime Factor
description: Return the smallest prime that divides the integer `n >= 2` (a prime `n` returns itself).
constraints: the answer is a prime number

title: Node Degree Lookup
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes (0 to n-1). `edges` lists the edges as flat pairs `[u0, v0, u1, v1, ...]`. Return the number of edges touching node `v`.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 20, at most 40 edges, no self loops or repeated edges

title: Even Degree Node Count
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes (0 to n-1) and `edges` as flat pairs `[u0, v0, u1, v1, ...]`. Return how many nodes have an even number of incident edges (zero counts as even).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 20, at most 40 edges, no self loops or repeated edges

title: Source Node Count
description: A directed graph has `n` nodes (0 to n-1) and `edges` as flat pairs `[from0, to0, from1, to1, ...]`. Return the number of nodes that have no incoming edge.
constraints: no self loops or repeated edges

title: Edge Between Nodes Check
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes and `edges` as flat pairs `[u0, v0, u1, v1, ...]`. Return `true` if nodes `a` and `b` are joined directly by an edge.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 20, at most 40 edges, no self loops or repeated edges

title: Leap Years In Range
description: Return how many leap years lie in the inclusive year range `[a, b]`. A year is leap if divisible by 4, except years divisible by 100 that are not divisible by 400.

examples.explanation: There are 1 leap year(s) in the range.
There are 0 leap year(s) in the range.

constraints: use the Gregorian rule for every year

title: Additive Persistence Steps
description: Repeatedly replace `n` by the sum of its decimal digits until a single digit remains. Return how many replacements were needed (`0` if `n` already has one digit).

title: Triangular Number Check
description: Return `true` if `n` is a triangular number, i.e. `n = 1 + 2 + ... + k` for some `k >= 0`.

title: Pronic Number Check
description: A pronic number is a product of two consecutive integers `k * (k + 1)` with `k >= 0`. Return `true` if `n` is pronic.

title: Letter Case Variants Count
description: Every letter of `s` may be written in lowercase or uppercase while digits stay fixed. Return how many distinct strings can be produced.
constraints: s has lowercase letters and digits only

title: Weighted Degree Of Node
description: A directed graph has `n` nodes and `edges` as flat triples `[from0, to0, w0, from1, to1, w1, ...]`. Return the total weight of all edges that start or end at node `v` (an edge touching `v` counts once).

examples.explanation: The edges touching v weigh 8 in total.
The edges touching v weigh 0 in total.

title: Page Navigation Trail Replay
description: A browser starts on page `0`. `ops` is a flat list of `(type, x)` pairs: type `0` visits page `x` (all forward history is discarded), type `1` goes back `x` steps (stopping at the first page), type `2` goes forward `x` steps (stopping at the latest page). Return the page the browser shows after all operations.

title: Aliquot Sum Equals Itself
description: A positive integer is perfect if it equals the sum of its proper divisors (all divisors smaller than itself). Return `true` if `n` is perfect.

title: Digit Power Fixed Point
description: A number is an Armstrong number if it equals the sum of each of its digits raised to the power of the number of digits. Return `true` if `n` is one.

title: Squarefree Numbers Count
description: A positive integer is squarefree if no perfect square larger than `1` divides it. Return how many squarefree numbers lie in `1..n`.

examples.explanation: There are 7 squarefree number(s) up to n.
There are 1 squarefree number(s) up to n.

title: Two-Factor Numbers Count
description: Count the integers in `2..n` that can be written as a product of exactly two primes (the two primes may be equal, e.g. `4 = 2 * 2` and `15 = 3 * 5`).

examples.explanation: 4 number(s) are products of exactly two primes.
0 number(s) are products of exactly two primes.

title: Divisor Count Running Total
description: Let `d(k)` be the number of positive divisors of `k`. Return `d(1) + d(2) + ... + d(n)`.

examples.explanation: The running total of divisor counts is 1.
The running total of divisor counts is 10.

constraints: the answer fits in a 64-bit integer

title: Perfect Power Count
description: A perfect power is a number `a^b` with integers `a >= 2` and `b >= 2`. Return how many distinct perfect powers lie in `2..n`.

examples.explanation: There are 3 perfect power(s) up to n.
There are 0 perfect power(s) up to n.

constraints: count each value once even if it has several representations

title: Smallest Number With Two Remainders
description: Given coprime moduli `m` and `n` and remainders `a < m`, `b < n`, return the smallest non-negative integer `x` with `x % m == a` and `x % n == b`.

title: Binomial Trailing Zeros
description: Return the number of trailing zero digits of the binomial coefficient `C(n, k)` written in decimal.

title: Pairs With Target XOR
description: Count the pairs of indices `i < j` such that `nums[i] XOR nums[j] == target`.

title: Pairs With Zero AND
description: Count the pairs of indices `i < j` such that `nums[i] AND nums[j] == 0`.

examples.explanation: There are 3 pair(s) whose AND is zero.
There are 0 pair(s) whose AND is zero.

title: Subarrays With AND Equal K
description: Count the contiguous non-empty subarrays whose bitwise AND of all elements equals `k`.

examples.explanation: 6 subarray(s) have AND equal to k.
2 subarray(s) have AND equal to k.

title: Maximum Subarray XOR
description: Return the largest XOR value obtainable from any non-empty contiguous subarray of `nums`.

title: Diagonal Sort Weighted Total
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. Sort every top-left to bottom-right diagonal in ascending order (from its top-left end). Then return the sum of `value * (position + 1)` over all cells, where `position` is the cell's index in the row-by-row layout.

examples.explanation: The weighted total after sorting diagonals is 90.
The weighted total after sorting diagonals is 5.

title: Zeroable By Line Toggles
description: `grid` is an `R x C` binary table stored row by row. In one move you may pick a whole row or a whole column and toggle every bit in it (0 becomes 1, 1 becomes 0). Return `true` if some sequence of moves turns the table into all zeros.

title: Richest Walk Through Mine
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row; `grid[i][j]` is the gold in a cell and `0` means the cell is blocked. Start at any non-empty cell, move up/down/left/right only into non-empty cells, never visit a cell twice, and collect the gold of every visited cell. Return the maximum gold collectable (`0` if every cell is blocked).
constraints: 0 <= grid[i] <= 100 and at most 25 cells are non-zero

title: Cheapest Matrix Product Order
description: A chain of `n` matrices is multiplied in order; matrix `i` has `dims[i]` rows and `dims[i + 1]` columns (so `dims.length = n + 1`). Multiplying an `a x b` matrix by a `b x c` matrix costs `a * b * c` scalar multiplications. Return the minimum total cost over all ways to parenthesize the product.

title: Fewest Hops Between Nodes
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes (0 to n-1) and `edges` as flat pairs `[u0, v0, u1, v1, ...]`. Return the minimum number of edges on a path from `a` to `b`, or `-1` if they are not connected.

examples.explanation: The shortest connection uses 2 edge(s) (-1 means none).
The shortest connection uses -1 edge(s) (-1 means none).

constraints: 1 <= n <= 20, at most 40 edges, no self loops or repeated edges

title: Nodes Within K Hops
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes (0 to n-1) and `edges` as flat pairs. Return how many nodes (including `s` itself) can be reached from `s` using at most `k` edges.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 20, at most 40 edges, no self loops or repeated edges

title: Network Diameter
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes and `edges` as flat pairs. If the graph is connected, return its diameter: the largest, over all node pairs, of the fewest edges needed to travel between them. If it is not connected return `-1`.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 20, at most 40 edges, no self loops or repeated edges

title: Central Node Count
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes and `edges` as flat pairs. The eccentricity of a node is its largest shortest-path distance to any other node. If the graph is connected, return how many nodes have the smallest eccentricity in the graph; otherwise return `-1`.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 20, at most 40 edges, no self loops or repeated edges
a single node is its own centre

title: Smallest Dependency Order
description: A directed graph has `n` tasks (0 to n-1); each pair `(u, v)` in the flat list `edges` means task `u` must come before task `v`. Return the lexicographically smallest valid ordering (compare as sequences of numbers) as the task ids joined by single spaces, or the word `none` if no valid ordering exists.
constraints: no self loops or repeated edges

title: Routes From First To Last Node
description: A directed acyclic graph has `n` nodes (0 to n-1) and `edges` as flat pairs `[from0, to0, ...]`. Return the number of different paths from node `0` to node `n - 1` (a graph with `n = 1` has exactly one path).
constraints: the graph has no cycles, self loops or repeated edges

title: Richest Cluster Total
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes; node `i` holds `values[i]`. `edges` lists the connections as flat pairs. A cluster is a maximal set of mutually reachable nodes. Return the largest total value held by any single cluster.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 20, values.length = n, at most 40 edges
-100 <= values[i] <= 100, no self loops or repeated edges

title: Money Loop Detection
description: A directed graph has `n` nodes and `edges` as flat triples `[from0, to0, w0, from1, to1, w1, ...]` where `w` may be negative. Return `true` if the graph contains a cycle whose total weight is negative (reachable or not from any particular start).
constraints: -5 <= w <= 10, no self loops, no repeated (from, to) pair

title: Spare Cables To Connect Network
description: `n` computers (0 to n-1) are wired by the cables in `edges` (flat pairs). In one move you may unplug any cable and reuse it between any two computers. Return the minimum moves needed to make all computers connected, or `-1` if there are not enough cables.
constraints: no self loops or repeated cables

title: Mutual Friend Triangles
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes and `edges` as flat pairs. Return the number of triangles: sets of three nodes that are all directly connected to each other.
constraints: no self loops or repeated edges

title: Kth Balanced Bracket String
description: Consider all valid strings made of `n` pairs of round brackets, sorted in dictionary order with `(` smaller than `)`. Return the `k`-th string (1-indexed), or the word `none` if there are fewer than `k` strings.

title: Knight Board Walk Count
description: A knight stands on square `(sr, sc)` of an `R x C` board (0-indexed). Return how many different sequences of exactly `L` knight moves keep it on the board (squares may be revisited).

title: Versioned Store Replay
description: `ops` is a flat list of quadruples `(type, key, value, time)`. Type `0` stores `value` under `key` at `time`; type `1` reads `key` as of `time` (the value whose store time is the latest one not after `time`, or `0` if none) and its `value` field is `0`. Store times strictly increase through the list. Return the sum of all values read.
constraints: 4 <= ops.length <= 400 and ops.length is a multiple of 4

title: Deepest Prerequisite Chain
description: A directed acyclic graph has `n` nodes (0 to n-1) and `edges` as flat pairs `[from0, to0, ...]`. Return the number of edges on the longest path in the graph (`0` if it has no edges).
constraints: the graph has no cycles, self loops or repeated edges

title: Dictionary Segmentation Count
description: `words` is a space-separated list of distinct dictionary words. Return the number of different ways to split the whole string `s` into a sequence of dictionary words (words may be reused).

examples.input: s = "catsanddog", words = "cat cats and sand dog"
examples.explanation: There are 2 way(s) to segment s.
There are 3 way(s) to segment s.

constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 30, 1 to 8 words, each of length 1 to 10

title: Distinct Prime Factor Total
description: For each `k` in `1..n` count how many different primes divide `k` (`1` has none). Return the sum of these counts.
constraints: count each distinct prime once per number

title: Smooth Number Count
description: A number is `p`-smooth if all of its prime factors are at most `p`. Return how many numbers in `1..n` are `p`-smooth (`1` always counts).

title: Two-Base Palindrome Count
description: Count the integers in `1..n` that read the same forwards and backwards both in decimal and in binary (no leading zeros).

examples.explanation: 5 number(s) are palindromes in both bases.
1 number(s) are palindromes in both bases.

constraints: binary form has no leading zeros

title: Halving Steps To One
description: In one step, an even `n` becomes `n / 2`; an odd `n` becomes either `n + 1` or `n - 1`. Return the minimum number of steps to reach `1`.

title: Leaderboard Replay
description: `ops` is a flat list of triples `(type, a, b)`. Type `0`: add `b` points to player `a` (new players start at 0). Type `1`: sum the points of the `a` highest-scoring players (all of them if fewer exist; `b = 0`). Type `2`: remove player `a` from the board (`b = 0`; nothing happens if absent). Return the sum of all type-1 answers.

examples.explanation: The top-score queries add up to 10.
The top-score queries add up to 0.

constraints: 3 <= ops.length <= 300 and ops.length is a multiple of 3

title: Running Median Replay
description: `ops` is a flat list of pairs `(type, x)`. Type `0` adds the number `x` to a collection. Type `1` (with `x = 0`) asks for the current median: the middle value when the count is odd, or the floor of the average of the two middle values when it is even. The collection is never empty at a query. Return the sum of all answers.

title: Transfer Ledger Replay
description: `balances[i]` is the money in account `i`. `ops` is a flat list of triples `(from, to, amount)`; a transfer happens only if the `from` account has at least `amount`, otherwise it is skipped. After all operations return the sum of `balance[i] * (i + 1)` over all accounts.
constraints: ops.length is a multiple of 3 and at most 150; accounts are valid and from != to; 1 <= amount <= 1000

title: Towns Within Travel Budget
description: A directed road network has `n` towns (0 to n-1) and `edges` as flat triples `[from0, to0, cost0, ...]`. Starting in town `0`, return how many towns (including town 0) can be reached with a total travel cost of at most `B`.

examples.explanation: 3 town(s) are reachable within the budget.
2 town(s) are reachable within the budget.

title: Largest Island After One Fill
description: `grid` is an `R x C` binary table stored row by row (`1` = land). You may change at most one `0` cell into land. Return the size of the largest island (group of land cells connected up/down/left/right) that can result.

examples.explanation: The largest island can reach size 3.
The largest island can reach size 4.

title: Diamond Neighbourhood Best Sum
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. For a centre cell `(i, j)` its diamond is every cell `(x, y)` inside the table with `|x - i| + |y - j| <= k`. Return the largest diamond sum over all centre cells.

title: Pairs With Given LCM
description: Return the number of pairs of positive integers `(a, b)` with `a <= b` whose least common multiple is exactly `n`.
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Lattice Points In Circle
description: Return the number of integer points `(x, y)` (including the boundary) with `x*x + y*y <= r*r`.

title: Digit Sum Multiple Count
description: Return how many integers in `1..n` have a decimal digit sum that is divisible by `k`.

title: Pairs With XOR In Range
description: Count the pairs of indices `i < j` for which `low <= nums[i] XOR nums[j] <= high`.

examples.explanation: 6 pair(s) have XOR in the range.
11 pair(s) have XOR in the range.

title: Fewest Signed Powers To Zero
description: In one operation you add or subtract any power of two (`1, 2, 4, 8, ...`) to the current value. Return the minimum number of operations to turn `n` into `0`.
constraints: powers of two may be reused

title: Submatrices With Target Sum
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row (values may be negative). Return the number of contiguous rectangular sub-tables whose cells add up to exactly `k`.

title: Multiplicative Order
description: Given `a` and `m` with `gcd(a, m) = 1`, return the smallest positive integer `k` such that `a^k` leaves remainder `1` when divided by `m`.

title: Primitive Root Count
description: A primitive root modulo `n` is a number `g` coprime to `n` whose powers `g^1, g^2, ...` hit every residue coprime to `n`. Return how many primitive roots exist among `1..n` (`0` if none).

examples.explanation: There are 2 primitive root(s) modulo n.
There are 0 primitive root(s) modulo n.

constraints: roots are counted among residues 1 to n (n itself is never coprime)

title: Monotone Paths With K Turns
description: On an `R x C` grid you walk from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell moving only right or down. A turn happens whenever two consecutive moves differ in direction. Return how many different paths have exactly `k` turns.

title: Fewest Arrow Edits To Cross
description: Each cell of an `R x C` table (stored row by row) holds an arrow: `1` right, `2` left, `3` down, `4` up. Starting at the top-left cell you follow the arrow of the cell you stand on. You may edit any cell's arrow at a cost of `1` each (a cell may be used more than once but needs editing only once). Return the minimum edits so that the walk can reach the bottom-right cell, moving only to cells inside the table.

title: Flood Wait Crossing
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table of terrain heights stored row by row. Water rises uniformly; at time `T` you may stand on, and walk (up/down/left/right) between, cells whose height is at most `T`. Starting in the top-left cell, return the earliest time `T` at which you can reach the bottom-right cell.

title: Runner-Up Spanning Tree Cost
description: An undirected weighted graph has `n` nodes and `edges` as flat triples `[u0, v0, w0, ...]`. Consider every spanning tree (set of `n - 1` edges connecting all nodes) and sort their total weights, keeping duplicates for different trees. Return the second smallest total, or `-1` if the graph has fewer than two spanning trees.

examples.explanation: The second cheapest spanning tree costs 4.
The second cheapest spanning tree costs -1.

constraints: 1 <= w <= 9, no self loops or repeated node pairs

title: Heaviest Non-Adjacent Node Set In Tree
description: A tree has `n` nodes (0 to n-1); node `i` has weight `values[i]`. `edges` lists its `n - 1` edges as flat pairs. Choose a set of nodes with no two directly connected and return the largest possible total weight.

title: Distance Sum Weighted Over Tree Nodes
description: A tree has `n` nodes (0 to n-1) and `edges` as flat pairs. For each node `i` let `S(i)` be the sum of distances (in edges) from `i` to every other node. Return the sum of `(i + 1) * S(i)` over all nodes.

title: Ancestor Meeting Point Total
description: A tree on nodes `0..n-1` is rooted at node `0`; `edges` lists its `n - 1` edges as flat pairs. `queries` is a flat list of pairs `(a, b)`. For each pair find their lowest common ancestor (the deepest node that lies on both root paths; a node is its own ancestor). Return the sum of the ids of these ancestors.
constraints: queries.length is even and at most 60; 0 <= a, b < n

title: Cable Network With Free Links
description: An undirected weighted graph has `n` nodes and `edges` as flat triples `[u0, v0, w0, ...]` (the cost of laying each cable). A promotion lets you lay at most `k` cables for free. Return the minimum total cost to connect all nodes, or `-1` if they cannot be connected.
constraints: 1 <= w <= 9, no self loops or repeated node pairs

title: Components After Each Removal Total
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes and `edges` as flat pairs; `order` is a permutation of the edge indices `0..m-1`. Edges are deleted one at a time following `order`. After each deletion count the connected components of the remaining graph. Return the sum of these counts over all `m` deletions (`0` if there are no edges).

examples.explanation: The component counts add up to 5.
The component counts add up to 5.

constraints: 1 <= n <= 20, at most 40 edges, no self loops or repeated edges
order contains each index 0..m-1 exactly once

title: Sliding Tile Fewest Moves
description: A `2 x 3` board holds the tiles `1..5` and one empty slot `0`, listed row by row. A move slides a tile that is next to the empty slot (up/down/left/right) into it. Return the fewest moves needed to reach `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0]`, or `-1` if it is impossible.

title: Fewest Bitmask Sets To Cover
description: The universe is `{0, ..., m-1}`. Each entry of `sets` is a bitmask: bit `i` set means that set contains element `i`. Return the fewest sets (each usable once, but using one twice never helps) whose union is the whole universe, or `-1` if impossible.

examples.explanation: The fewest sets needed: 3 (-1 means impossible).
The fewest sets needed: 2 (-1 means impossible).

title: Magic Square Completions
description: A `3 x 3` board (row by row) is partly filled: `0` marks an empty cell, other cells hold distinct digits `1..9`. A completed board is magic if it uses each of `1..9` exactly once and every row, column and both diagonals add up to `15`. Return how many magic boards agree with all the filled cells.
constraints: each cell is 0 to 9 and non-zero values are distinct

title: Merged Runs Count Replay
description: `ops` is a flat list of pairs `(type, x)`. Type `0` inserts the integer `x` into a set (duplicates are ignored). Type `1` (with `x = 0`) asks how many maximal runs of consecutive integers the set currently forms, for example `{1,2,3,7,8,10}` forms `3` runs. Return the sum of all answers.

examples.explanation: The run counts add up to 1.
The run counts add up to 3.

constraints: 0 <= x <= 1000 for insertions; type is 0 or 1

title: Fewest Row Swaps To Staircase
description: `grid` is an `n x n` binary table stored row by row. In one move you swap two adjacent rows. The table is valid when every cell above the main diagonal is `0`. Return the minimum number of moves to make it valid, or `-1` if that is impossible.

title: Widest Route Bottleneck
description: An undirected road network has `n` towns (0 to n-1) and `edges` as flat triples `[u0, v0, capacity0, ...]`. The bottleneck of a route is the smallest capacity along it. Return the largest bottleneck achievable by any route from town `0` to town `n - 1`, or `0` if they are not connected.
constraints: 1 <= capacity <= 9, no self loops or repeated node pairs

title: Letter Cutout Sticker Count
description: `stickers` is a space-separated list of words, each an unlimited supply of stickers. Using any number of stickers you may cut out single letters and rearrange them freely. Return the fewest stickers needed to spell the string `target`, or `-1` if it cannot be spelled.
constraints: 1 <= number of stickers <= 6, each of length 1 to 8

title: Max-OR Shortest Reach Sum
description: For every start index `i`, find the shortest subarray beginning at `i` whose bitwise OR equals the largest OR achievable by any subarray starting at `i`. Return the sum of those shortest lengths over all `i`.

examples.explanation: The window lengths add up to 11.
The window lengths add up to 3.
